answer: Shared-Anchor Registration Windows. Each agent identity must anchor its first transaction to a public registration window opened at dawn, and windows close after a fixed interval. Within a window, only one identity per verified network endpoint may register; a second attempt from that endpoint forces the first identity to pay a timber forfeit equal to its full registration deposit. Attackers mass-registering identities therefore lose deposits proportional to endpoints they control, while honest agents pay only once per window.
